Feature: GPIO Register Access and Reset Verification
Test Description: Validate GPIO registers gp0_gpio_8 through gp0_gpio_27 for correct reset defaults and masked write/read behavior using standard data patterns.
Meta Test Description: The test iterates over a fixed list of GPIO registers (GP0_GPIO_8..GP0_GPIO_27). First, it reads each register after reset and compares the value with an expected default defined in the test definitions. Next, it performs masked write-read verification using a pattern set {0xFFFFFFFF, 0xAAAAAAAA, 0x55555555, 0xF5F5F5F5, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xFFFF0000}. For each pattern and each register: the write value is masked with the per-register write mask, written to the register, then the register is read and masked with the per-register read mask. The masked readback is compared against the expected masked value. Any mismatch is logged as an error. A soft reset check routine exists in the code but is disabled.
Remarks: Ensure the GPIO block is powered, clocked, and released from reset before access. Avoid concurrent accesses to gp0_gpio_8..gp0_gpio_27 during validation.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1. Initialize the platform so the GPIO module is powered, clocked, and out of reset.
2. Read each register gp0_gpio_8 through gp0_gpio_27 and verify it matches its documented reset default.
3. For each of these registers, perform write/read checks using standard data patterns while respecting the register's write and read masks.
4. Record any mismatches and continue until all registers and patterns are covered.
5. Report PASS if all reset and masked write/read checks succeed; otherwise report FAIL.
Meta Test Steps / Procedure:
- Build an ordered list of target registers: [GP0_GPIO_8..GP0_GPIO_27].
- Reset/default verification loop:
  - For each register r in the list: val = read(r); exp = default_reset_val[r]; if (val != exp) { log_error(r, val, exp); set_fail(); }
- Masked write-read verification:
  - patterns = {0xFFFFFFFF, 0xAAAAAAAA, 0x55555555, 0xF5F5F5F5, 0xA5A5A5A5, 0xFFFF0000}
  - For each register r in the list:
    - wr_mask = write_mask[r]; rd_mask = read_mask[r]
    - For each p in patterns:
      - wr_val = (p & wr_mask)
      - write(r, wr_val)
      - rd_val = read(r)
      - rd_chk = (rd_val & rd_mask)
      - exp_chk = ((p & wr_mask) & rd_mask)
      - if (rd_chk != exp_chk) { log_error(r, p, wr_mask, rd_mask, rd_val, exp_chk); set_fail(); }
- A soft_reset_chk() function exists but is disabled; no reset action is performed.
- Final result: PASS if no mismatches are detected across all registers and patterns; otherwise FAIL.
Impacted Registers: gp0_gpio_8, gp0_gpio_9, gp0_gpio_10, gp0_gpio_11, gp0_gpio_12, gp0_gpio_13, gp0_gpio_14, gp0_gpio_15, gp0_gpio_16, gp0_gpio_17, gp0_gpio_18, gp0_gpio_19, gp0_gpio_20, gp0_gpio_21, gp0_gpio_22, gp0_gpio_23, gp0_gpio_24, gp0_gpio_25, gp0_gpio_26, gp0_gpio_27
Meta Impacted Registers: GP0_GPIO_8, GP0_GPIO_9, GP0_GPIO_10, GP0_GPIO_11, GP0_GPIO_12, GP0_GPIO_13, GP0_GPIO_14, GP0_GPIO_15, GP0_GPIO_16, GP0_GPIO_17, GP0_GPIO_18, GP0_GPIO_19, GP0_GPIO_20, GP0_GPIO_21, GP0_GPIO_22, GP0_GPIO_23, GP0_GPIO_24, GP0_GPIO_25, GP0_GPIO_26, GP0_GPIO_27
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: Pass if each register's reset value equals its expected default and, for all patterns and registers, the read value (after applying the read mask) equals the value written (after applying the write mask and then the read mask). Any deviation is a failure.
Meta Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
- Reset check: For each r, read(r) == default_reset_val[r]; else FAIL and log r, val, exp.
- Write/read check: For each r and each pattern p: wr = (p & write_mask[r]); write(r, wr); rd = read(r); rd_m = (rd & read_mask[r]); exp = ((p & write_mask[r]) & read_mask[r]); if (rd_m != exp) -> FAIL and log r, p, wr_mask, rd_mask, rd, exp.
- Overall: PASS only if no mismatches are detected in any register or pattern.

Test Description: Validate negative-edge interrupt functionality on all GPIO pads by enabling negedge detection, generating high-to-low transitions, verifying interrupt assertion, and clearing per-pin interrupt status.
Meta Test Description: The test configures all GPIO pads for negative-edge interrupt detection and enables GPIO interrupt generation. It sets pad direction/output control (as required by the platform) to generate a high-to-low transition on each pad sequentially. Global interrupts are enabled and the ISR (Default_IRQHandler) is expected to service the pad interrupts. For each pad: drive the pad high, then low to create a negative edge; confirm the corresponding bit is set in the raw interrupt status; and clear the per-pin interrupt via the interrupt status clear register. The test also ensures the interrupt is actually taken (via ISR bookkeeping) and validates that after clearing, no residual status remains.
Remarks: Ensure the GPIO interrupt is enabled at the system-level interrupt controller and global IRQs are unmasked. Confirm the GPIO clock and power are enabled. Before starting, clear any pending GPIO interrupt status using the interrupt status clear register. Provide a controllable stimulus path to toggle pads high-to-low. Restore output/data configuration to a safe state after testing.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1. Initialize the platform and enable the GPIO block clock and power.
2. Configure all target GPIO pads for negative-edge interrupt detection and enable GPIO interrupts.
3. Prepare pad control so that each pad can be driven high then low to create a negative edge (or arrange an equivalent external stimulus).
4. Enable global interrupts and ensure the system interrupt controller routes the GPIO IRQ to the CPU.
5. For each pad: drive it high, then drive it low to generate a negative edge.
6. Verify that a GPIO interrupt occurs and the corresponding raw interrupt status bit is set for that pad.
7. Clear the per-pad interrupt using the interrupt status clear register and confirm the raw status bit is cleared.
8. Repeat steps 5-7 for all pads under test and report overall pass/fail.
Meta Test Steps / Procedure:
- Enable clocks/power for the GPIO IP.
- Program NEG_EDGE_EN to enable negative-edge detection for all target pads (bit-per-pad).
- Program INT_EN to enable GPIO interrupt generation (pad-level and any group/mask as required).
- Configure DIR and DATA_OUT (or equivalent I/O control) to allow generating transitions on each pad under test.
- Enable CPU/GIC interrupts (e.g., IRQ 87/88) and unmask global IRQs; install/enable Default_IRQHandler.
- For pad index i over all pads under test:
  - Drive pad i to logic '1' via DATA_OUT (if loopback/self-stimulus is used).
  - Drive pad i to logic '0' via DATA_OUT to create a negative edge.
  - In ISR: record interrupt occurrence and optionally latch the pad index (implementation-specific bookkeeping).
  - Read INT_RAW_STAT and check bit i == 1.
  - Write INT_STAT_CLR with bit i = 1 to clear the interrupt.
  - Read INT_RAW_STAT and check bit i == 0.
- After all pads: confirm ISR count/events match expected number of generated edges.
- Any mismatch or missing interrupt results in failure.
Impacted Registers: NEG_EDGE_EN, INT_EN, INT_RAW_STAT, INT_STAT_CLR, GRP_MASK, DATA_OUT, DIR
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: Pass if for every tested pad a negative edge triggers a GPIO interrupt, the corresponding raw interrupt status bit is set, the interrupt is serviced, and the status bit is cleared by writing to the interrupt status clear register. Fail if any pad does not assert an interrupt on a negative edge or if the status cannot be cleared.
Meta Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
- For each pad i: after generating a high-to-low transition, INT_RAW_STAT[i] must read as 1 and the ISR must be taken. After writing INT_STAT_CLR[i]=1, INT_RAW_STAT[i] must read as 0.
- Aggregated ISR/event counts must equal the number of generated pad transitions.
- Any deviation (no interrupt, wrong status bit, or uncleared status) results in FAIL.

Test Description: Validate positive-edge interrupt functionality across all GPIO pads by enabling positive-edge detection, generating low-to-high transitions, verifying interrupt assertion, and clearing per-pin interrupt status.
Meta Test Description: This test configures all GPIO pads to trigger interrupts on a positive (rising) edge. It enables GPIO interrupt generation and sets pad direction/output control to produce low-to-high transitions sequentially on every pad under test. Global CPU interrupts are enabled so the default interrupt handler services GPIO interrupts. For each pad: the test creates a rising edge, confirms the corresponding bit in the raw interrupt status is set, and then clears the interrupt using the per-pin interrupt status clear register. Group/aggregate interrupt status is also checked (if present) to ensure it asserts on pad events and de-asserts after all underlying pad interrupts are cleared.
Remarks: Ensure the GPIO block power and clock are enabled and global interrupts are unmasked. Clear any pending GPIO interrupt status before starting. Provide a safe and controllable stimulus path to toggle pads from low to high. Restore pad configuration to a safe state after completion.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1. Power and clock the GPIO module and clear any pending GPIO interrupt status.
2. Configure all target pads for positive-edge interrupt detection and enable GPIO interrupt generation.
3. Prepare I/O control so each pad under test can be driven from low to high (or arrange equivalent external stimulus).
4. Enable global interrupts and ensure the system interrupt controller routes GPIO interrupts to the CPU.
5. For each pad: drive it low, then drive it high to create a positive edge and observe an interrupt.
6. Verify the corresponding raw interrupt status is set for that pad and that the interrupt is serviced.
7. Clear the per-pad interrupt and confirm the raw status is cleared; verify any group/aggregate status de-asserts when appropriate.
8. Repeat for all pads and declare pass only if all pads assert and clear as expected.
Meta Test Steps / Procedure:
- Initialize: enable GPIO IP clock/power; write INT_STAT_CLR with all-ones mask to clear pending pad interrupts; optionally read GROUP_INT_STATUS to confirm no pending group status.
- Configure detection: program POS_EDGE_EN with bit-per-pad enables for all pads under test; program INT_EN (and GROUP_INT_ENABLE if used) to allow GPIO interrupts to propagate.
- I/O control: set DIR to output for pads used to self-stimulate; ensure DATA_OUT is driven to 0 prior to edge generation.
- Enable CPU interrupts: unmask global IRQs; install/enable Default_IRQHandler; ensure GPIO IRQ is enabled in the system controller.
- For each pad index i: drive DATA_OUT[i] from 0 to 1 to create a rising edge; verify INT_RAW_STAT[i] == 1; clear via INT_STAT_CLR[i] = 1; verify INT_RAW_STAT[i] == 0.
- Optionally validate GROUP_INT_STATUS assertion/de-assertion.
- Finalize by restoring pad configuration to a safe state.
Impacted Registers: POS_EDGE_EN, INT_EN, INT_RAW_STAT, INT_STAT_CLR, GROUP_INT_ENABLE, GROUP_INT_STATUS, DATA_OUT, DIR
Meta Impacted Registers: POS_EDGE_EN, INT_EN, INT_RAW_STAT, INT_STAT_CLR, GROUP_INT_ENABLE, GROUP_INT_STATUS, DATA_OUT, DIR
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: Pass if every tested pad's rising edge sets its raw interrupt status, an interrupt is serviced, and the status clears when the interrupt status clear register is written. Any pad failing to assert on a rising edge or failing to clear results in a fail.
Meta Validation / Acceptance Criteria: - For each pad i: after a low-to-high transition, INT_RAW_STAT[i] must read 1 and the ISR must be taken. After writing INT_STAT_CLR[i]=1, INT_RAW_STAT[i] must read 0. If group status is used, it must de-assert after clearing all relevant pad interrupts.
